subject: math
explanation: When dividing powers with the same base, subtract the exponents: nᵃ ÷ nᵇ = nᵃ⁻ᵇ (n ≠ 0). Example: 2¹⁰⁰ ÷ 2²⁵ = 2⁷⁵. Cancelling b factors from a factors leaves a − b factors. This law explains negative exponents: 2⁰ ÷ 2⁵ = 2⁻⁵ = 1/32. It also works when exponents are negative: 2⁻² ÷ 2⁻⁵ = 2³ = 8.

brainstorming.question: Why can n not be 0 in nᵃ ÷ nᵇ?
brainstorming.answer: If n = 0, the denominator 0ᵇ (b > 0) is 0, giving division by zero — undefined.

brainstorming.question: What happens when a = b?
brainstorming.answer: nᵃ ÷ nᵃ = n⁰ = 1 — any non-zero base to power 0 is 1.

brainstorming.question: How does quotient law create negative exponents?
brainstorming.answer: 2³ ÷ 2⁵ = 2⁻² = 1/4 — subtracting gives a negative exponent meaning reciprocal.

misconceptions.correct: Division by zero is undefined — n must be non-zero.
Same exponent different bases: (6/2)⁴ = 3⁴ — quotient law on bases, not subtracting unlike bases.

realLifeConnections.title: Comparing cell counts
realLifeConnections.description: If bacteria double daily, ratio after 100 days vs 25 days is 2¹⁰⁰ ÷ 2²⁵ = 2⁷⁵.

realLifeConnections.title: Signal attenuation
realLifeConnections.description: Signal halving each km: after 10 km vs 3 km, strength ratio is 2¹⁰ ÷ 2³ = 2⁷.

realLifeConnections.title: Storage tiers
realLifeConnections.description: Ratio of 1 TB (2⁴⁰ bytes) to 1 GB (2³⁰ bytes) is 2¹⁰.

realLifeConnections.title: Simplifying fractions
realLifeConnections.description: 10⁴/5⁴ = (10/5)⁴ = 2⁴ — quotient of powers with same exponent.

activities.title: Cancel and count
activities.instructions: Write 2⁵/2² as (2×2×2×2×2)/(2×2). Cancel two 2s and count three left → 2³.

activities.title: Quotient law relay
activities.instructions: Teams simplify 5⁷÷5⁴, 9⁻⁷÷9⁴, 2⁻²÷2⁻⁵. Pass the answer to the next teammate.

activities.title: Zero exponent discovery
activities.instructions: Compute 3⁴÷3⁴, 7⁶÷7⁶, aⁿ÷aⁿ. What pattern do you notice?

quiz.question: nᵃ ÷ nᵃ equals:
quiz.explanation: a - a = 0, and n⁰ = 1 for n ≠ 0.

quiz.question: Why must n ≠ 0?
quiz.explanation: 0ᵇ = 0 for b > 0, causing division by zero.
